request:
I sell provisions at Makola market and I want to keep track of my stock. For each item I want to save its name, how many I have, and the level at which I consider it to be running low. When I sell some of an item the quantity should go down, but I must not be able to sell more than I have. When new goods arrive I record a restock and the quantity goes up. The amount sold or restocked must always be more than zero. I want to see all my items, look at one item, and see a list of the items that are at or below their low level so I know what to buy.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Do you sell items in whole units only (like 5 bags), or sometimes in parts (like 2.5 kg)?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: When you add a new item, should the name be unique, so you can't enter the same item twice?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Do you want a history of each sale and restock (date and amount), or only the current quantity for each item?
A: Not needed for now; I only need the current quantity.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app import app

c = TestClient(app)


def make(name="Rice", q=10, low=3):
    r = c.post("/items", json={"name": name, "quantity": q, "low_level": low})
    assert r.status_code == 201
    return r.json()


def test_create_get_list():
    i = make()
    assert c.get(f"/items/{i['id']}").json()["name"] == "Rice"
    assert any(x["id"] == i["id"] for x in c.get("/items").json())
    assert c.get("/items/999999").status_code == 404


def test_invalid_create():
    assert c.post("/items", json={"name": "", "quantity": 1, "low_level": 1}).status_code == 422
    assert c.post("/items", json={"name": "x", "quantity": -1, "low_level": 1}).status_code == 422
    assert c.post("/items", json={"name": "x"}).status_code == 422


def test_sell():
    i = make()
    r = c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/sell", json={"amount": 4})
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["quantity"] == 6
    assert c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/sell", json={"amount": 7}).status_code == 400
    assert c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/sell", json={"amount": 0}).status_code == 422
    assert c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/sell", json={"amount": -1}).status_code == 422
    assert c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/sell", json={"amount": 6}).json()["quantity"] == 0
    assert c.post("/items/999999/sell", json={"amount": 1}).status_code == 404


def test_restock():
    i = make()
    assert c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/restock", json={"amount": 5}).json()["quantity"] == 15
    assert c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/restock", json={"amount": 0}).status_code == 422
    assert c.post("/items/999999/restock", json={"amount": 1}).status_code == 404


def test_low_stock():
    a = make("Low", 3, 3)
    b = make("Fine", 10, 3)
    ids = [x["id"] for x in c.get("/items/low-stock").json()]
    assert a["id"] in ids and b["id"] not in ids
    c.post(f"/items/{b['id']}/sell", json={"amount": 8})
    ids = [x["id"] for x in c.get("/items/low-stock").json()]
    assert b["id"] in ids

I wrote `app.py` and `tests/test_app.py`. All 5 tests pass. Data is saved in a SQLite file called `stock.db`.

Each item has an id, a name, a quantity and a low level. I used whole units only and allowed repeated names, since you had no preference on either.

- `POST /items` adds an item. You send `name`, `quantity` and `low_level`. The name can't be empty, and the numbers can't be negative.
- `GET /items` lists all items.
- `GET /items/{id}` shows one item. It returns 404 if there is no such item.
- `GET /items/low-stock` lists the items at or below their low level, so you know what to buy.
- `POST /items/{id}/sell` takes `{"amount": n}` and lowers the quantity. It returns 400 if you try to sell more than you have.
- `POST /items/{id}/restock` takes `{"amount": n}` and raises the quantity.

An amount of zero or less is refused with 422 on both sell and restock.
